---
title: "India gridded rainfall - poking around"
output: html_notebook
---

IMD 0.25 deg daily rainfall, 1901-2025. Grain is cell-day (~4,964 land cells).
Big file, so keep the heavy summarising inside arrow and only `collect()` the
small results.

```{r}
require(tidyverse)
require(arrow)

require(ellmer)

if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"))) {
  stop("Set OPENAI_API_KEY in .Renviron, restart R, then rerun.")
}

ds <- open_dataset("rainfall_parquet")
ds
```

What does coverage actually look like?

```{r}
ds %>%
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    start = min(date),
    end = max(date),
    cells = n_distinct(paste(lat, lon))
  ) %>%
  collect()
```

All-India daily mean = average rainfall across every land cell on a given day.
That's the number that should trace out the monsoon.

```{r}
ds %>%
  group_by(year, date) %>%
  summarise(mean_mm = mean(rainfall_mm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) -> daily
```

Overlay every year on a day-of-year axis, highlight 2025 against the other 124.

```{r}
daily %>%
  mutate(
    doy = yday(date),
    this_year = year == 2025
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(doy, mean_mm, group = year)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = this_year, linewidth = this_year), alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey80", "#1b7a7a")) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(0.2, 0.7)) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 200,
    y = Inf,
    label = "2025",
    vjust = 1.5,
    colour = "#1b7a7a",
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "2025 sits inside the usual monsoon envelope",
    x = "day of year",
    y = "all-India mean mm/day"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Is India getting wetter over 125 years? Sum the daily mean within each year to
get an annual accumulation for the average cell.

```{r}
daily %>%
  summarise(annual_mm = sum(mean_mm), .by = year) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, annual_mm)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(size = 0.6, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, colour = "#1b7a7a", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "No obvious long-run trend in all-India annual rainfall",
    x = NULL,
    y = "annual mm (avg cell)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

The all-India average hides everything interesting. Pick one place. Grab its
cell from the lookup.

```{r}
lookup <- read_parquet("cell_lookup.parquet")

lookup %>%
  filter(str_detect(name, "Bengaluru|Bangalore")) %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  head(3)
```

```{r}
blr <- lookup %>%
  filter(str_detect(name, "Bengaluru|Bangalore")) %>%
  slice_max(population, n = 1)

ds %>%
  filter(abs(lat - blr$cell_lat) < 0.01, abs(lon - blr$cell_lon) < 0.01) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), doy = yday(date), yr = year(date)) -> blr_rain
```

Median day-of-year rainfall for that cell - when does its monsoon show up?

```{r}
blr_rain %>%
  summarise(med_mm = median(rainfall_mm), .by = doy) %>%
  ggplot(aes(doy, med_mm)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1b7a7a", width = 1) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(
      blr$name,
      ": median daily rainfall by day of year (1901-2025)"
    ),
    x = "day of year",
    y = "median mm"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Back to the whole map: where did it actually rain in 2025? Annual total per cell.

```{r}
ds %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  group_by(lat, lon) %>%
  summarise(annual_mm = sum(rainfall_mm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  collect() -> map2025

map2025 %>%
  ggplot(aes(lon, lat, fill = annual_mm)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "mm") +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(
    title = "2025 rainfall: the Western Ghats and Northeast light up",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```


How has Bengaluru rainfall moved over the years? Annual totals are noisy, so
keep the individual years but add a broad trend.

```{r}
blr_rain %>%
  summarise(annual_mm = sum(rainfall_mm), .by = year) -> blr_yearly

blr_yearly %>%
  filter(annual_mm %in% range(annual_mm)) %>%
  mutate(
    note = if_else(annual_mm == max(annual_mm), "Wettest", "Driest"),
    label = paste0(
      note,
      "\n",
      year,
      " · ",
      scales::comma(round(annual_mm)),
      " mm"
    )
  ) -> blr_extremes

blr_yearly %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, annual_mm)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey40", size = 0.9) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, colour = "#1b7a7a", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = blr_extremes, colour = "#1b7a7a", size = 2) +
  geom_text(
    data = blr_extremes,
    aes(label = label, vjust = if_else(note == "Wettest", -0.7, 1.5)),
    colour = "#1b7a7a",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.2,
    lineheight = 0.9,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.16))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bengaluru's annual rainfall, 1901-2025",
    subtitle = "Annual total at the nearest 0.25° grid cell",
    x = NULL,
    y = "annual rainfall (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

What about the big cities together? Nine gives us a clean 3 x 3, and Bengaluru
can stay in the comparison rather than sitting off on its own.

```{r}
tribble(
  ~city       , ~pattern                  ,
  "Delhi"     , "^(New )?Delhi$"          ,
  "Mumbai"    , "^Mumbai$"                ,
  "Kolkata"   , "^Kolkata$"               ,
  "Chennai"   , "^Chennai$"               ,
  "Bengaluru" , "^(Bengaluru|Bangalore)$" ,
  "Hyderabad" , "^Hyderabad$"             ,
  "Ahmedabad" , "^Ahmedabad$"             ,
  "Pune"      , "^Pune$"                  ,
  "Jaipur"    , "^Jaipur$"
) -> city_patterns

city_patterns %>%
  mutate(
    cell = map2(city, pattern, function(city, pattern) {
      lookup %>%
        filter(str_detect(name, regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE))) %>%
        slice_max(population, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
        transmute(city = city, cell_lat, cell_lon)
    })
  ) %>%
  select(cell) %>%
  unnest(cell) -> city_cells

city_cells
```

Do the expensive annual sum before collecting. The separate latitude/longitude
filters may admit a few crossed cells; the exact join removes them afterwards.

```{r}
ds %>%
  filter(
    lat %in% city_cells$cell_lat,
    lon %in% city_cells$cell_lon
  ) %>%
  group_by(lat, lon, year) %>%
  summarise(annual_mm = sum(rainfall_mm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  collect() %>%
  inner_join(
    city_cells,
    by = c("lat" = "cell_lat", "lon" = "cell_lon")
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    city = factor(city, levels = city_patterns$city),
    year,
    annual_mm
  ) -> city_yearly
```

A straight slope is too crude here. Give the model five-year means and ask it
to describe the shape: rises, falls, plateaus, reversals, and the recent move.
One call for all nine cities.

```{r, fig.width=14, fig.height=12, out.width='100%'}
city_yearly %>%
  mutate(period_start = 1901 + 5 * ((year - 1901) %/% 5)) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_mm = round(mean(annual_mm)),
    .by = c(city, period_start)
  ) %>%
  arrange(city, period_start) -> city_trend_input

paste(
  "Describe the long-run rainfall shape for each Indian city below.",
  "The values are five-year means of annual rainfall in millimetres.",
  "Focus on multi-decade rises, falls, plateaus, reversals, and recent direction.",
  "Do not reduce the series to one slope. Do not claim significance or causation.",
  "Write one plain-English sentence per city, at most 12 words.",
  paste(
    capture.output(write.csv(city_trend_input, row.names = FALSE)),
    collapse = "\n"
  ),
  sep = "\n"
) -> trend_prompt

ellmer::type_array(
  ellmer::type_object(
    city = ellmer::type_enum(city_patterns$city, "City name"),
    trend = ellmer::type_string(
      "Concise description of the multi-decade rainfall shape; at most 12 words"
    )
  ),
  description = "Exactly one trend description for each of the nine cities"
) -> city_trend_type

trend_chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-5.6-luna")

trend_chat$chat_structured(
  trend_prompt,
  type = city_trend_type
) %>%
  mutate(city = as.character(city)) -> city_trends

stopifnot(
  nrow(city_trends) == nrow(city_patterns),
  setequal(city_trends$city, city_patterns$city)
)

city_yearly %>%
  summarise(avg_mm = mean(annual_mm), .by = city) %>%
  mutate(city = as.character(city)) %>%
  left_join(city_trends, by = "city") %>%
  arrange(match(city, city_patterns$city)) %>%
  mutate(
    facet_label = paste0(
      city,
      " · avg ",
      scales::comma(round(avg_mm)),
      " mm/year\n",
      stringr::str_wrap(trend, width = 100)
    ),
    facet_label = factor(facet_label, levels = facet_label)
  ) -> city_stats

city_yearly %>%
  mutate(city = as.character(city)) %>%
  left_join(city_stats, by = "city") -> city_yearly_plot

city_yearly_plot %>%
  group_by(city, facet_label) %>%
  filter(annual_mm %in% range(annual_mm)) %>%
  mutate(
    note = if_else(annual_mm == max(annual_mm), "Wettest", "Driest"),
    label = paste0(
      note,
      "\n",
      year,
      " · ",
      scales::comma(round(annual_mm)),
      " mm"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() -> city_extremes

city_yearly_plot %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, annual_mm)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.65) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey40", size = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, colour = "#1b7a7a", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = city_extremes, colour = "#1b7a7a", size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(
    data = city_extremes,
    aes(label = label, vjust = if_else(note == "Wettest", -0.7, 1.5)),
    colour = "#1b7a7a",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.3,
    lineheight = 1,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(facet_label), ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.12, 0.18))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual rainfall across nine major Indian cities",
    subtitle = stringr::str_wrap(
      "Panel headings show the 1901–2025 average and an LLM reading of the trend; scales vary by city",
      width = 130
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "annual rainfall (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 12,
      lineheight = 1.1,
      margin = margin(t = 5, b = 14)
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10.5, colour = "grey20"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold",
      lineheight = 1,
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(y = 8)
    )
  )
```

## City rainfall since 1951

Repeat the nine-city comparison for post-1950 data only. Five-year periods now
begin in 1951, so the trend summaries and panel averages use 1951–2025 throughout.

```{r, fig.width=14, fig.height=12, out.width='100%'}
city_yearly %>%
  filter(year > 1950) -> city_yearly_post1950

city_yearly_post1950 %>%
  mutate(period_start = 1951 + 5 * ((year - 1951) %/% 5)) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_mm = round(mean(annual_mm)),
    .by = c(city, period_start)
  ) %>%
  arrange(city, period_start) -> city_trend_input_post1950

paste(
  "Describe the post-1950 rainfall shape for each Indian city below.",
  "The values are five-year means of annual rainfall in millimetres for 1951–2025.",
  "Focus on multi-decade rises, falls, plateaus, reversals, and recent direction.",
  "Do not reduce the series to one slope. Do not claim significance or causation.",
  "Write one plain-English sentence per city, at most 12 words.",
  paste(
    capture.output(write.csv(city_trend_input_post1950, row.names = FALSE)),
    collapse = "\n"
  ),
  sep = "\n"
) -> trend_prompt_post1950

trend_chat$chat_structured(
  trend_prompt_post1950,
  type = city_trend_type
) %>%
  mutate(city = as.character(city)) -> city_trends_post1950

stopifnot(
  nrow(city_trends_post1950) == nrow(city_patterns),
  setequal(city_trends_post1950$city, city_patterns$city)
)

city_yearly_post1950 %>%
  summarise(avg_mm = mean(annual_mm), .by = city) %>%
  mutate(city = as.character(city)) %>%
  left_join(city_trends_post1950, by = "city") %>%
  arrange(match(city, city_patterns$city)) %>%
  mutate(
    facet_label = paste0(
      city,
      " · avg ",
      scales::comma(round(avg_mm)),
      " mm/year\n",
      stringr::str_wrap(trend, width = 100)
    ),
    facet_label = factor(facet_label, levels = facet_label)
  ) -> city_stats_post1950

city_yearly_post1950 %>%
  mutate(city = as.character(city)) %>%
  left_join(city_stats_post1950, by = "city") -> city_yearly_plot_post1950

city_yearly_plot_post1950 %>%
  group_by(city, facet_label) %>%
  filter(annual_mm %in% range(annual_mm)) %>%
  mutate(
    note = if_else(annual_mm == max(annual_mm), "Wettest", "Driest"),
    label = paste0(
      note,
      "\n",
      year,
      " · ",
      scales::comma(round(annual_mm)),
      " mm"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() -> city_extremes_post1950

city_yearly_plot_post1950 %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, annual_mm)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.65) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey40", size = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, colour = "#1b7a7a", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = city_extremes_post1950, colour = "#1b7a7a", size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(
    data = city_extremes_post1950,
    aes(label = label, vjust = if_else(note == "Wettest", -0.7, 1.5)),
    colour = "#1b7a7a",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.3,
    lineheight = 1,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(facet_label), ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.12, 0.18))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual rainfall across nine major Indian cities since 1951",
    subtitle = stringr::str_wrap(
      "Panel headings show the 1951–2025 average and an LLM reading of the post-1950 trend; scales vary by city",
      width = 130
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "annual rainfall (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 12,
      lineheight = 1.1,
      margin = margin(t = 5, b = 14)
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10.5, colour = "grey20"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold",
      lineheight = 1,
      hjust = 0,

```
